body:
## Pull request overview

This PR improves Timeline and Gantt UX by adding configurable styling variants to the Timeline components and addressing Gantt accessibility/mobile information density gaps.

**Changes:**
- `plugin-timeline`: Introduces `cva`-based variants for `TimelineItem` density and `TimelineMarker` semantic statuses (and exports the variant helpers).
- `plugin-gantt`: Adds `aria-label`s to icon-only toolbar buttons and renders a mobile-only inline date range badge under task titles.
- Adds/updates lockfile + introduces new test coverage for both packages.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 6 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| pnpm-lock.yaml | Adds `class-variance-authority` for `plugin-timeline` and includes additional lockfile churn (incl. removal of `examples/hotcrm/*` importer entries). |
| packages/plugin-timeline/src/index.tsx | Adds `cva` variant definitions for `TimelineItem` and `TimelineMarker`, and exports the variant functions. |
| packages/plugin-timeline/src/__tests__/timeline-variants.test.tsx | New tests validating density + marker variants and overrides. |
| packages/plugin-timeline/package.json | Adds `class-variance-authority` dependency. |
| packages/plugin-gantt/src/GanttView.tsx | Adds `aria-label`s and a mobile-only date range line under the task title. |
| packages/plugin-gantt/src/__tests__/GanttView.test.tsx | New tests for aria-labels and mobile date badge rendering. |
</details>


<details>
<summary>Files not reviewed (1)</summary>

* **pnpm-lock.yaml**: Language not supported
</details>

The lockfile includes substantial unrelated churn (e.g., removal of `examples/hotcrm/packages/*` importers and pino@10-related snapshots) that isn't described in the PR and makes review/risk assessment harder. If intentional, please note why in the PR description; otherwise consider regenerating `pnpm-lock.yaml` to keep it scoped to the Timeline/Gantt changes.

`TimelineMarker`'s `default` and `in-progress` variants are both blue and differ only by a small border shade change, which can make status meaning ambiguous (especially for color-blind users). Consider making `default` a neutral (e.g., slate/gray) so `in-progress` is clearly distinguishable.
